title: Though sacrifice is withheld, votive offerings and dedicatory gifts fill Saints’ named churches and chapels
source_text: XIV. Praeterea licet in Ecclesia Romana sacrificia Sanctis non offerantur, illis tamen variae fiunt oblationes, & solemne est eis donaria consecrare, in memoriam beneficiorum quae putantur ab illis accepta, sive per eos impetrata: qualia plurima visuntur in templis & sacellis de illorum nomine vocatis.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, although in the Roman Church sacrifices are not offered to the Saints, yet various oblations are made to them, and it is solemn to consecrate gifts to them, in memory of benefits which are thought received from them, or obtained through them: of which kind very many are seen in temples and chapels called by their name.
pass_b_english: Sacrifice aside, Rome still loads Saints with oblations and consecrated gifts.
These mark benefits thought received from or through them—crowding their named shrines.

choices.why: Material tokens hung in Saints’ shrines.
